A.explanation: Upward momentum $100v\sin60^{\circ}$ with $v = 4.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is only about half the downward $800\text{ g m s}^{-1}$, so vertical momentum is not conserved.

B.explanation: Vertical components $50v_1\sin60^{\circ}+50v_2\sin60^{\circ}$ balance $100 \times 8\text{ g m s}^{-1}$, giving $v_1 = v_2 \approx 9.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: With $v = 14\text{ m s}^{-1}$ the total upward momentum exceeds the downward momentum of the $100\text{ g}$ piece, so net vertical momentum would be upward not zero.

D.explanation: Using $\cos60^{\circ}$ instead of $\sin60^{\circ}$ for the vertical component to the horizontal dashed line gives $v = 8/\cos60^{\circ} = 16\text{ m s}^{-1}$, which overestimates the upward momentum.

hints: Notice the firework is stationary before the explosion, so total vector momentum after must be zero and the $100\text{ g}$ piece carries $800\text{ g m s}^{-1}$ downward at $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Connect the $60^{\circ}$ angles to the horizontal dashed line to the vertical components: each $50\text{ g}$ piece contributes $50v\sin60^{\circ}$ upward.
Set total upward momentum equal to total downward momentum and solve $100v\sin60^{\circ} = 100 \times 8$ for $v$, checking that horizontal components cancel by symmetry.
walkthrough: Identify the data: two $50\text{ g}$ pieces move up-left and up-right at $60^{\circ}$ to the horizontal with speeds $v_1$ and $v_2$, and one $100\text{ g}$ piece moves vertically down at $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
State the rule: initial momentum is zero, so vector sum of final momenta is zero. Horizontal momentum must cancel and vertical momentum must balance.
Use horizontal balance: leftward $50v_1\cos60^{\circ}$ must equal rightward $50v_2\cos60^{\circ}$. With equal masses and equal angles this requires $v_1 = v_2 = v$.
Use vertical balance: upward $50v\sin60^{\circ} + 50v\sin60^{\circ} = 100v\sin60^{\circ}$ must equal downward $100 \times 8\text{ g m s}^{-1}$.
Substitute and solve: $100v\sin60^{\circ} = 800$, so $v = 8/\sin60^{\circ} = 8/0.866 \approx 9.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with unit $\text{m s}^{-1}$. This is option B.
